faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium RF Grounding Spring Finger suitable for RF grounding spring contact finger (Nitinol)?
faq.a: Titanium RF Grounding Spring Finger uses Grade 2 CP-Ti because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address chamber shield operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium RF Grounding Spring Finger?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium RF Grounding Spring Finger is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for rf grounding spring requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium RF Grounding Spring Finger require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. rf grounding spring components require Electropolishing Ra <0.25um + UHP DI cascade rinse with particle count verification per MIL-STD-1246 Class 1 — tailored for rf grounding spring application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium RF Grounding Spring Finger shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium RF Grounding Spring Finger includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet rf grounding spring specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Ground finger / RF spring chamber shield components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
